title: Perdón
setting: You said something in front of five people that you should not have. It is the next morning.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué andás haciendo aquí tan temprano?
steps.en: And what are you doing here so early?

options.es: Vine a hablar con vos. Sobre lo de ayer.
options.en: I came to talk to you. About yesterday.
options.feedback: Naming why you came, straight away, before the coffee. That is the shape an apology takes here.
Nobody passes by at seven. He knows why you are here and now you both have to pretend.

options.en: Nothing, I came to say hello.
options.feedback: The one thing that makes an apology worse is arriving without it.

options.es: Me pasé. Lo siento, de verdad.
options.en: I went too far. I am sorry, honestly.
options.feedback: Short, no explanation attached. A long apology turns into an excuse and both of you know it.
The si makes it conditional, as though it might not have happened. It did.

options.es: Es que yo no sabía nada de eso.
options.en: The thing is I did not know anything about that.
options.feedback: That is a defence, not an apology. Do the apology first, if at all.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.en: It is all right, man. It is over.

options.es: Gracias. No lo vuelvo a hacer.
options.en: Thank you. I will not do it again.
options.feedback: Accepted without arguing that it was nothing. The promise is short enough to be believed.
Agreed. He offered you the door and you walked out without saying anything.

options.en: So you were not angry then.
options.feedback: Making him say it again is asking him to do the hard part twice.

options.es: Dale. ¿Cómo va lo de la casa?
options.en: Right. How is the house thing going?
options.feedback: He offered coffee instead of forgiveness, which is how it is done, and you moved to something ordinary. That is the repair finished.
Accepted. Leaving the silence there means one of you has to fill it with the same subject again.

options.en: So we are all right now, are we not?
options.feedback: The coffee was the answer. Asking for it in words takes it back apart.
